messages:
sam: Hey team — escalated ticket from @ava: embeddings endpoint returning wrong vector size after customer enabled a custom quantization profile. Customer saw 1536 -> 512 collapse. Error in their app: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 512". They claim it only happens when they use our int8 quant profile.

ava: Confirming — we flipped quant_profile to "int8-speed" to save costs. Calls were fine before. After change, embeddings are shorter and some downstream indexing breaks. We have sample request + response.

miles: Can you paste the exact request body and headers? Also which model were they calling? Some models have multiple embedding heads.

ava: Sure:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large-v2","input":"test sentence","quant_profile":"int8-speed","batch_size":8}'

Response body (truncated):
{
  "data": [ { "embedding": [ /* 512 floats here */ ] } ],
  "model": "open-embed-large-v2"
}

sam: Thanks. Repro attempt notes:
- model: open-embed-large-v2 (expected dim 1536)
- quant_profile: int8-speed
- batch_size: 8

jia: Interesting. Two immediate hypotheses:
1) Quant profile is selecting a different model variant (e.g., a 512-d projection) under routing fallback.
2) Our quantized loader path has a bug that swaps the projection matrix when using per-tensor int8 packing, leading to a truncated output.

luci: I can check routing logs. If the request routes to a compat model variant (open-embed-large-v2-int8-compat) that was created with an alternative head, that would explain it.

deploy-bot: [info] route-selection: req=1851234567 model=open-embed-large-v2 -> instance=open-embed-large-v2-int8-speed-01 region=us-west-2

sam: deploy-bot log shows int8-speed instance used, so not an unexpected model swap.

miles: Can we get the raw base64 model fingerprint and quant metadata? The customer report suggests the quantizer changes the projection dims. If the quantized file lacks a named tensor (e.g., "proj.weight") we may fall back to default smaller projection at runtime.

jia: I'll pull the model artifacts from the instance. In the meantime, quick repro script for support to validate locally:

```bash
python repro_embed.py <<'PY'
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key='RED_XXXX')
for q in ['none','fp16','int8-speed','int8-compat']:
    r = c.embeddings.create(model='open-embed-large-v2', input='hello world', quant_profile=q, batch_size=1)
    print(q, len(r.data[0].embedding))
PY
```

ava: We ran similar and saw lengths: none=1536, fp16=1536, int8-speed=512, int8-compat=1536. So int8-speed is the odd one out.

sam: Good repro. That rules out tokenization.

jia: I fetched the artifact metadata. Notes:
- open-embed-large-v2-int8-speed.tar contains quant_state.json showing "projection_shape": [512, 1536] and "packed": true.
- loader logs contain a warning: "fallback to packed-int8-single-head" when loading "proj.weight"

luci: That loader warning wasn't expected. Looks like for int8-speed we run a packing transformer that assumes a faster 512-d projection for export to some accelerator. That suggests our packer created a smaller on-disk tensor but left model metadata claiming 1536. At load time runtime slices to 512 and downstream code didn't update embedding dim.

sam: So customer sees 512-length vectors but our API advertises 1536; downstream indexers error out. Need mitigation and a permanent fix.

miles: Short-term mitigation: intercept embeddings responses and include an additional header or field that reports actual vector length. We can also validate at serve time and return 400 if quant_profile produces a different dim than model spec. Quick patch suggestion for the hosted API proxy: if len(embedding) != model_spec.dim then reject or include "actual_embedding_dim" in response.

jia: Agreed. I'll open a hotfix branch to add a response field "actual_embedding_dim" and a warning log. Also add a server-side check to block unsafe quant profiles for publicly advertised model dims.

ava: Customer needs a workaround now — what to tell them?

sam: For now ask them to switch to "int8-compat" or "fp16". If they must use int8-speed for cost, they can update their indexer to accept 512-d vectors (not ideal). We'll offer migration help.

ava: I'll pass that along. Customer also asked if this could be a billing issue (charges for wrong model).

luci: No billing discrepancy — billing uses the requested model id and quant profile slug; cost calc doesn't assume dimension. But we should flag this for billing to be aware if we change upstream pricing for int8-speed.

deploy-bot: [info] ticket-attach: 1851234567 -> eng-ml #3872

jia: Action items I'm taking:
- Roll a quick hosted-proxy patch to include actual_embedding_dim and reject mismatched dims (ETA 2hrs).
- Add unit test that loads packed int8 artifacts and verifies projection shape matches model spec (ETA end of day).
- Root cause: quant packer produced 512-d projection artifact for speed profile; need to adjust packer metadata and loader compatibility.

miles: I'll update the support KB with the workaround and sample repro script (link to internal doc).

sam: Thanks. I'll update the customer with the workaround (use int8-compat/fp16) and give ETA for the fix.

ava: Appreciate it. One more ask: can we add a temporary API flag to force the server to return full-dim unquantized embeddings even if quant_profile requested? Some customers want correctness over cost.

jia: We can add a "force_unquantized": true param that bypasses quantized path for hosted models (must be behind permission). I'll include that as a follow-up task (security review required).

sam: Perfect. I'll close the loop with the customer after the patch deploy.

luci: Patch deployed to canary. deploy-bot shows no errors on startup. Please monitor logs for any 400s from the new dim-check.

deploy-bot: [info] canary-deploy: service=embeddings-proxy env=canary version=2026.3.15-quick-dim-check

sam: Monitoring now. If we see no regressions we'll rollout to prod and notify billing + docs to mark int8-speed as lower-dim in the interim.

ava: Thanks all :thumbsup:
